meta.title: Mock brand-vs-rival shopper profiles (SYNTHETIC demo data)
meta.source: analytics-assistant-be/demo_mock/out (generator seed 20260602): visitor_observation.csv (179,336 visits), receipt_line.csv (484,120 lines / 172,292 receipts), product.csv (206 SKUs), store.csv, segment.csv
meta.period: June 2026 (synthetic), 10 CZ/SK sites; tobacco sold only at the 6 convenience sites
meta.warning: SYNTHETIC. Every number here is an output of a hand-written generator (spec_pos.py, spec_segments.py, generate.py, generate_pos.py). Use only as illustrative teaser material, never as a market fact.
meta.suppression: Any cell (segment, store, age band, daypart, tier, co-purchase, residual brand share) with fewer than 25 distinct shoppers is reported as "<25". Whole groups with n_buyers < 25 are suppressed.

definitions.buyer: distinct person_id with >=1 receipt line of the group's brand(s) inside the group's category set. person_id is one visit (no repeat-visitor identity in the mock), so n_buyers == n_receipts in practice.
definitions.segment_mix: % of classified buyers (Low-Signal excluded). index = segment share among group buyers / segment share among all buyers of the category x100.
definitions.store_mix_index: store share among group buyers / store share among category buyers x100
definitions.age: decade bands from visitor_observation.age; mean_age uses midpoints 10s=16, 20s=25, 30s=35, 40s=45, 50s=55, 60s+=67; 'unknown' excluded. 10s band included (task asked for 20s+ bands).
definitions.promo: a line is on promo when amount_gross/quantity < 0.97 x list_price. Only 7 brands had June promo windows (monster, big shock, semtex, nivea, dove, lay's, own brand); tobacco is never discounted. Every other brand is 0% by construction.
definitions.mean_receipt_czk: mean total receipt value (all lines) of the group's buyers vs category buyers
definitions.copurchase: share of group buyers whose receipt also has category/brand X (group's own categories excluded) vs same share among category buyers -> index; min 25 co-buyers; 'counter' food-service lines excluded; own brand keyed by category
definitions.rest_of_basket_tier_spend_share: share of the buyer's spend OUTSIDE the group's categories and outside tobacco that is private label / premium tier
definitions.tuned: true when spec_pos.py / generate.py give the brand an explicit per-segment bias (or tob_brand bias). false = only tier appetite, listing (convenience vs drugstore) or noise can differentiate it. Structural drivers are named in tuning_basis.

generator_caveats: merchandise_brand (brands seen carried) is populated for 27.3% of visitors but covers only 22 brands: 6 energy (red bull, monster, big shock, nocco, celsius, semtex), 8 bodycare (nivea, dove, rexona, adidas, old spice, vichy, la roche-posay, own brand) and 8 'other FMCG' brands drawn uniformly at random (coca-cola, pepsi, kofola, snickers, lay's, kinder, milka, mattoni). No tobacco, beer, ice cream, haircare, oral-care, water other than Mattoni, or sports-nutrition brand is ever carried, so the residual cannot be computed for those.

The put-back mechanic is a flat 18% coin-flip per carried brand (SHELF_ABANDONMENT) with NO substitution logic: 'what they bought instead' is simply the carrier's normal segment basket. Brand-to-brand differences in put-back rate come from (a) whether the carrier's segment would buy the brand anyway and (b) listing (Vichy/La Roche-Posay are not stocked at convenience sites, so 100% of those carriers there 'do not buy').
Bodycare items are only ever carried by 4 segments (Suburban Parent, Office Professional, Value Senior, Everyday Mainstream); other segments' bodycare carry ladders are never used.
Gender is driven only by segment, never by brand: Old Spice or adidas buyers are ~46-47% women because drugstore shoppers are. Do not use gender contrasts for gendered brands.
Sports nutrition is bought only by Gym Regulars (it is only in their category list), so segment contrasts inside sports nutrition are impossible.
Beer is never in the Long-Haul Transit basket, so no driver ever buys Birell (non-alcoholic).
Ice cream is only in the Suburban Parent, Young Streetwear and City-Break Tourist baskets.

Corridor Commuters and Office Professionals have no salty snacks or soft drinks in their category lists; the only crisps/soft drinks they buy are the carried-and-forced Lay's / Coca-Cola / Pepsi / Kofola, which creates artificial brand monopolies inside those segments.
Listing drives several 'untuned' contrasts: Fanta, Bonaqua, Twix, beer and all tobacco are convenience-only; Elseve, Syoss, Sensodyne, Kerastase, Vichy/LRP, most skincare are drugstore-only.
HTP/vape devices are drawn independently of the consumable brand on the receipt (DEVICE_ATTACH), so device_on_receipt_pct overstates 'starters' for small brands.

residual.description: 'Picked it up and did not buy it': shoppers seen carrying brand X (merchandise_brand) who have a receipt without any X line. by_segment/by_format give the put-back rate. residual_bought_instead = brands bought in X's core category by those put-back shoppers (% of put-back shoppers who bought anything in the category; index vs brand penetration among all category buyers). reverse_rival_buyers_seen_with_X = of all buyers of rival Y, how many were seen with X and did not buy X.

promo_uplift.description: Per segment: penetration of the promoted brand among that segment's category buyers on promo days vs all other June days, the ratio (uplift), and the share of the segment's spend on the brand that was discounted. Heatwave (days 8-12) overlaps the Nivea and Big Shock windows.

cigarette_buyers_private_label_elsewhere.description: Private-label share of NON-tobacco spend (excl. counter food) among buyers of the cigarette brand, split by segment
